edges.description: The accumulated deoxysphingoid bases are directly toxic to cultured sensory and motor neurons.
The same metabolites reach the retina, where they cause photoreceptor death in human retinal organoids.
Degeneration of the longest sensory axons produces the length-dependent distal sensory deficit that opens the clinical picture.
Small-fibre loss removes protective nociception.
The same small-fibre loss removes thermal perception, which is what makes unnoticed burns possible.
Degenerating sensory neurons also generate positive sensory phenomena, the characteristic shooting or lancinating pains.
Loss of the distal-most sensory terminals, measurable on skin biopsy, is the histological correlate of the small-fibre deficit.
Loss of large myelinated sensory fibres is what abolishes sensory nerve action potentials on nerve conduction studies.
Motor axons degenerate as well, which is why weakness follows the sensory deficit in most patients despite the disease's name.
Denervation of distal limb muscles produces wasting.
Retinal deoxysphingolipid toxicity is the proposed basis of the macular telangiectasia type 2 seen in most examined HSAN1 patients.
Sensory loss removes the warning that would prevent injury to the feet and hands.
Unperceived trauma to insensate extremities.
Unperceived burns to insensate extremities.
Unprotected injuries on insensate feet break down into chronic ulcers.
Repeated unperceived trauma to insensate joints destroys them.
Chronic ulcers become infected and the infection reaches bone.
Osteomyelitis that cannot be controlled is treated by amputation.
Raising alanine relative to serine gives the mutant enzyme more of the substrate it wrongly prefers, increasing 1-deoxysphingolipid formation.

edges.description: Human sensory neurons carrying the patient genotype show reduced neurite outgrowth, disrupted nodal complexes in myelinating coculture and, by six months, myelin breakdown.

edges.description: Age-dependent degeneration of sensory and motor axons on the background of a disease-causing human allele, with the small-fibre component apparent only at later ages.
edges.limitations: The model overexpresses a human transgene rather than carrying a heterozygous endogenous variant, so the mutant dose is not the human one. The impairments were described as mild at the age first reported, and the mouse does not reproduce the acral ulceration and amputation that dominate human morbidity.

edges.description: The mouse makes the same atypical deoxysphingoid bases as patients, and they respond to dietary substrate in the expected direction.
The knock-in raises the disease metabolite in plasma at the endogenous gene dose, and the elevation is reversible by silencing the mutant allele.
At the ages studied the mouse shows no prominent neurophysiological or pathological abnormality, although the human S331F phenotype is severe and early in onset.
edges.limitations: The mismatch is at least partly one of timing: the authors compare it with the C133W transgenic, where no distinct neuropathy appeared until adulthood, and their experiments were designed around young adults. But as studied, this model supports the biochemical arm of the mechanism and not the degeneration it is supposed to cause, so an efficacy claim resting on the metabolite alone in this model is a surrogate one.

nodes.description: 1-deoxysphinganine and 1-deoxymethylsphinganine lack the C1 hydroxyl group of a canonical sphingoid base. That hydroxyl is required both for conversion into complex sphingolipids and for entry into the normal degradation route, so these metabolites accumulate rather than turning over. They are elevated in the plasma of patients carrying several different SPTLC1 alleles, which makes this node the disease's accessible biomarker as well as its mechanism.

nodes.description: Preclinical only. Because the disease is caused by a product the mutant allele makes rather than by loss of the normal one, silencing the mutant transcript and leaving the wild-type allele intact is mechanistically the right target. GalNAc-conjugated locked-nucleic-acid gapmer antisense oligonucleotides against the p.S331F allele achieved over 90% mutant transcript silencing in liver and dorsal root ganglia of S331F mice, lowered blood 1-deoxysphingoid bases and reversed the aberrant dorsal-root-ganglion gene expression. No human study has been performed, and the construct is allele specific, so it would have to be remade for each variant.

nodes.description: Surgical fusion of joints destroyed by neuropathic arthropathy.

The mutant enzyme's output depends on which amino acid is available to it, so the balance between L-alanine and L-serine in the diet sets how much of the toxic metabolite is made. This is the basis of the L-serine treatment and, in the opposite direction, of the alanine-enriched diet that worsened the mouse phenotype. It is recorded here as a modifier of an inherited disease, not as a cause: the evidence is a mouse feeding experiment and a cell-culture titration, and no dietary exposure has been shown to cause or worsen the human disease.

It is, and most of the changes are prevented by L-serine.

nodes.description: Substrate competition rather than enzyme replacement: supplying the canonical substrate in excess pushes the mutant enzyme back towards serine and away from alanine and glycine, lowering production of the neurotoxic deoxysphingolipids. It is the only disease-modifying treatment tested in a randomised trial in this disease. At 400 mg/kg/day for a year the treated group improved on the Charcot-Marie-Tooth Neuropathy Score relative to placebo while deoxysphinganine fell, with no serious treatment-related adverse effects.

nodes.description: Serine palmitoyltransferase catalyses the condensation of palmitoyl-CoA with L-serine, the first and rate-limiting step of de novo sphingolipid synthesis. HSAN1A variants in the SPTLC1 subunit enhance the enzyme's activation of L-alanine and of glycine as alternative substrates, so the mutant enzyme makes products the wild-type enzyme makes only in trace amounts. Kinetic work on C133W found wild-type and mutant enzymes to have similar affinities for both serine and alanine, locating the defect in activation of alanine rather than in substrate binding, which is why the variant is curated as neomorphic rather than as a loss of function.

nodes.description: Deoxysphingoid bases are toxic to primary sensory and motor neurons in a dose- and time-dependent way, with disturbed endoplasmic-reticulum and mitochondrial calcium handling and early loss of mitochondrial membrane potential as proximate cellular effects, and with disturbed neurofilament structure in neurites. Degeneration is length-dependent, so the longest axons in the lower limbs fail first, which is why the clinical picture begins in the feet and why epidermal innervation is lost at the distal leg before the thigh.

nodes.description: A CRISPR-generated knock-in carrying the mutation at the endogenous locus, rather than a transgene, and therefore at the human gene dose. It reproduces the biochemistry faithfully: plasma 1-deoxysphingolipids are raised at every age measured, highest at postnatal day 7 and falling with age, and they drop on allele-specific silencing. It does not reproduce the neuropathy at the ages studied, which is why it is curated with both a RECAPITULATES and a FAILS_TO_RECAPITULATE link. Transcriptomics in its dorsal root ganglia implicates mitochondrial pathways, consistent with the calcium and mitochondrial findings in cultured neurons.

nodes.description: Mice ubiquitously overexpressing the human C133W mutant subunit develop an age-dependent sensory and motor phenotype with loss of large myelinated axons in dorsal and ventral roots, and at later ages a distal small-fibre neuropathy. Crossing them with mice overexpressing wild-type SPTLC1 largely reverses the phenotype, and heterozygous Sptlc1 knockout mice with reduced SPT activity are normal, so the model supports a toxic product rather than lost enzyme activity. It is the model in which dietary serine and alanine were shown to move the metabolite and the phenotype in opposite directions.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant SPTLC1 dominantly inhibits serine palmitoyltransferase activity in vivo and confers an age-dependent neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: We report here that SPTLC1(C133W) mice develop age-dependent weight loss and mild sensory and motor impairments.
